Text:
‎{{c1::وعَلَيكُم السَّلامُ}}

{{c2::And upon you peace}} — the reply to the Islamic greeting
Back Extra:
Cue: MSA — wa calaykum as-salaam

Distinguish: the reply is the greeting turned around — assalaamu calaykum becomes wa calaykum as-salaam. Dr. Khouri: "Just flip them."

Pitfall: the opening wa is the "and" of "and upon you peace" — Dr. Khouri told the class not to worry if you drop it.

Ex: Levantine [sound:arabic_vocab_lingco_wa_alaykum_shaami.mp3]
audio_source: lingco-formal (Alif Baa U2 row 6) — Dr. Khouri never says this phrase in isolation on the recording; every instance is inside an English sentence
evidence: slide 'Reply to greeting! (Islamic greeting)' at 00:56:35; drilled 00:58:00

Text:
‎{{c1::أسكُن}}

{{c2::I live}} — "___ in the city of Lynchburg"
Back Extra:
Cue: MSA — askun

Ex: askun fii madiinat Lynchburg — "I live in the city of Lynchburg," the sentence Dr. Khouri built on the board.

Pitfall: this verb is NOT in Alif Baa's Unit 1 list. She added it in class on 27 Aug: "This is not in the list. Add it to the list."
audio_source: khouri 01:11:50, modelled alone right after "say it after me"

Text:
‎{{c1::تشرفنا}}

{{c2::Nice to meet you}} — the line that closes an introduction
Back Extra:
Cue: MSA — tasharafna, as Dr. Khouri spells it on her slide.

Ex: you say it after your name, your city and where you live — it closes the introduction, and the thank-you exchange follows.

Pitfall: not in Alif Baa's Unit 1 list — she pulled it forward so the conversation can actually be finished.

Ex: book audio — Formal [sound:arabic_vocab_lingco_tasharafna_formal.mp3] · Levantine [sound:arabic_vocab_lingco_tasharafna_shaami.mp3]

Cue: MSA — shukran

Distinguish: shukran opens on shiin (sh), not the emphatic Saad (S). Dr. Khouri's slide writes it "Shukran" with a capital S as ordinary sentence styling — that capital is NOT her emphatic marker.

Ex: in the Tuesday exchange your partner says this back to your tasharafna.

Ex: book audio — Formal [sound:arabic_vocab_lingco_shukran_formal.mp3] · Levantine [sound:arabic_vocab_lingco_shukran_shaami.mp3]

Text:
‎{{c1::عفواً}}

{{c2::You're welcome}} — the last word of the intro exchange
Back Extra:
Cue: MSA — cafwan

Pitfall: cafwan opens on cayn, the same throat sound as in calaykum. Dr. Khouri's trick: say "ah", then start to shock yourself — but only a little.

Ex: book audio — Formal [sound:arabic_vocab_lingco_afwan_formal.mp3]
